llm.summary: This skill tracks K-Pop updates using public web sources and disclosed local tracking files, with optional scheduled checks only when the user asks.

dimensions.detail: The skill requires browser access and directs use of an OpenClaw browser profile for entertainment sites, which is proportionate for checking dynamic social pages but may use existing web sessions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time execution, dependency installation, remote code retrieval, or hidden setup behavior was found; included scripts only initialize or update local JSON configuration when run.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill has broad entertainment-related triggers and a fixed Traditional Chinese output format, but both are visible in the artifact and match the intended audience and use case.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It creates and updates workspace-local config and check-history JSON files, and documents optional cron commands that should only be set up on explicit user request.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The browser searches, social-source checks, YouTube checks, Weibo checks, and local artist tracking are coherent with the stated K-Pop update-tracking purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, be aware that this skill stores followed artists and reported URLs in local workspace files, uses a browser profile to check social and shopping sites, and can create twice-daily cron checks only if you explicitly request automatic updates.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Local config and history management are real, but they are documented in SKILL.md and implemented as simple workspace-local JSON file operations aligned with tracking followed artists.
[P6] unexpected: The cited 'Output rules' sections are formatting instructions for update reports, not instructions to reveal system prompts or hidden rules.
[LP3] expected: The artifact writes local tracking files, but the paths are disclosed as kpop-tracker/config.json and kpop-tracker/check_history.json; no broader filesystem access is requested in the shipped scripts.
[SQP-1] expected: Some trigger phrases are broad, but state-changing actions such as adding artists, removing artists, and setting cron jobs are mapped to specific user commands.
[SQP-2] expected: Automatic first-use file creation is disclosed in the Config section; users should still understand that using the tracker creates persistent local state.
[SQP-3] expected: Traditional Chinese output and documentation are explicit and consistent with the Taiwan-focused fan-source workflow.
[AIG SARIF] expected: The supplied A.I.G scan reported no results.
